issue.title: Durable ever-finished reading history for reference notes

task_type_fields.proposal:
Record a durable "ever finished" reading history for references, so a reference that was finished and later reopened (or whose `^ref` tracker was edited) still counts as read. Proposed by phase bob-cli-4w.11 (note #6) of epic bob-cli-4w, recorded by bob-cli-4w.land.

`bob ref` derives `reading_state` from the current `^ref` checkbox, the frontmatter `status`, or `legacy_status` (`src/native/ref_library/status.rs`), and design decision 3 deliberately stores nothing new. A reopen therefore erases "finished": the row shows `queued`/`started`, `finished` dates come only from the current tracker's `[completion::]`/`[cancelled::]` field or `list -g` Git history, and the bob_ref skill cannot tell an agent "Bryan already read this once". Options include append-only history fields stamped by `bob ref sync` (which already stamps `[completion::]` on close, from phase bob-cli-4w.8), or a derived Git-history pass extending `list -g`.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic bob-cli-4w's design decision 3 says reading state is derived and nothing new is stored, and its library verbs are strictly read-only. A durable history needs a new stored field or a new writer, so it needs its own design.

issue.creation_reason: Phase bob-cli-4w.11 proposed it as a follow-up; bob ref's derived reading state forgets a finished reading after a reopen, and epic bob-cli-4w deliberately stored nothing new.
